claims.text: Genesis 1 repeatedly moves from divine speech to appearance or action, evaluation, distinction, assignment, blessing, evening, and morning.
One passage presents humanity collectively as male and female with image, blessing, and rule; the other narrows to dust, breath, garden, command, aloneness, formation, recognition, and one flesh.
Exodus grounds weekly Sabbath in God’s completed work, while Hebrews cites the seventh day inside an argument that still speaks of entering rest.
The narrative moves from permission, boundary, unashamed relation, and garden life to covering, hiding, blame, pain, toil, mortality, exile, and guarded access.
The later writings select created order, boundaries, creatures, human limits, witness, provision, dependence, and renewal for different literary purposes.
John says all things came through the Word and joins creation to life and light; Colossians says all things were created through and for Christ and hold together in him.
Genesis describes completed work as very good; Romans describes creation subjected to futility, groaning, and waiting for freedom from corruption.
Genesis first places river and tree within the garden, then guards the tree of life after exile; Revelation places river, tree, healing, throne, and unending light within the city.
